utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Better in what way?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, how should I describe it? Well, I just thought it would be better for me, so that's why I moved. I thought they were better organised, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: How many members of the El Mujahedin Detachment were there at the time you moved into that unit?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the exact number; perhaps, 15 or 20 at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell the Court what the -- what the makeup was of that unit? Was it made up of persons not of Bosnian citizenship, or a mixture of some foreign fighters and some Bosnian citizens?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: There were foreign Bosnian fighters [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what do you mean by "foreign Bosnian fighters"?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, I had Arabs in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. So there were Bosnian and foreign fighters; is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just for the sake of the transcript, the witness said "foreign and Bosnian fighters" and the transcript states "foreign Bosnian fighters." There's no actual link between the two. The witness made a clear distinction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic, for that assistance. Madam Sartorio, I guess that clears your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, I don't need to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you recall what the ratio was at the time between the Bosnian and the foreign soldiers, in terms of the numbers?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: At the beginning?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, there weren't many Arabs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, what was required of you to move into that unit?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you have to receive any official permission from the 306th Mountain Brigade to transfer into that unit?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't need anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you were never considered to have deserted, for instance, the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina when you moved into that unit?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, I didn't really pay much attention to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I'm glad that the witness said -- has answered. I don't want to influence the witness. But if the Prosecution could avoid leading the witness, it would be good. This was a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And are you saying it's water under the bridge, there's nothing you can do about it, but you still record your objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can rephrase the question, if you'd like.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness has answered the question. However, I'd appreciate it if the Prosecution could avoid asking questions that imply that the witness has made a claim that he hasn't actually made. But the witness has already said he knew nothing about that, so I withdrew my objection. But I would appreciate it if the Prosecution could avoid putting leading questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Madam Sartorio, you hear the concern of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, were you ever disciplined for any reason for leaving the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: When you joined the unit in May of 1993, who was in charge of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, Haris was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And where was the command post?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: In Poljanice.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And was the command post located in one building?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, there were three houses there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And were these three houses owned by the El Mujahed Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know who -- did you hear about where these houses had come from, who had occupied these houses previously?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the Serbs were not living in those houses at the time the El Mujahed Detachment moved into them, were they?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: That's correct. There was no one there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know if anyone gave permission to the El Mujahed Detachment to occupy those houses?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: As far as I know -- well, I don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, in terms of the -- I guess for the term "foreign fighters," to be distinguished from the Bosnian-Herzegovinian citizens who were members of the El Mujahed Detachment, did the foreign fighters speak the Bosnian language?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: At the time, they didn't, those who were there when I arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Were you able to understand them when they were speaking?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you receive any classes or lessons from the El Mujahed Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, we had some instructions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what were these instructions on?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, religious instruction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May I just get some clarity?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said, sir, you didn't understand them when they spoke. How did you understand their religious instruction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We had a translator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: What was the name of the translator?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Abu Malik, a Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, did the -- over time, did the unit -- excuse me, did the El Mujahed Detachment grow?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And in terms of the numbers just prior to, say, any operation that you conducted by the El Mujahed Detachment, approximately, what were the numbers of the members?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know the precise number, but there were not many of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Were there 50?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: There weren't that many.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Were there more than ten?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Were there more than 20?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, let's say around 20, 30.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sorry. Excuse me. Twenty or 30, that's your answer?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: More or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I would like to show the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. I just want to understand this number: "20 or 30." Is this the number of the entire El Mujahed Detachment, inclusive of both foreigners and locals, or is it the foreign members only?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness what has been marked and entered into evidence Exhibit number 78. If we can put it up on the screen, it's PT2949. It was PT2949, and e-court page number is 161 to 162. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is it up on your screen?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is that page 161 to 162, e-court pages? It's supposed to be ERN 0365-5060.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, my case manager just gave me a number that may be of some assistance, P02949 C. I don't see it, Your Honour. I don't know what's going on with e-court. That's not the right number.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecutor, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that it, Madam Sartorio?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Prosecutor, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm looking, Your Honour. Yes, that's it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: We'll be using this double page and then the next page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like you to look at these two pages, and if you can, tell me what this is.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: It bears my first and last name, date of birth, my place of residence in Travnik Municipality. Also, it indicates where I served the army, in Niksic, and when I was seconded to Ulcinj.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And in paragraph 19, the places that you served, are those correct?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And are the dates of services next to those places, are those correct dates?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes. September, I think so, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Number 28, would you look at the writing, what's next to number 28. On the left-hand side of the left page, second from the top or third from the top, it says "Number 28." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do see. Military exercises, the military post, and the place.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when does it say that you served in the military? What are your starting dates and what are your completion dates?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, the initial date is the 4th of April, 1992 until the 14th of May, 1993. That was when I was in the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, if you look at the second entry and you go all the way over to the right, doesn't it --

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: And the second note, that is when I went to the El Mujahed Detachment from the 15th of May, 1993 to the 27th of December, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So these dates listed on this document, did they represent the dates that you served in these different units?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions about this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: We would like to tender it -- well, it's tendered as an exhibit, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think, yes, it is tendered. Thank you very much, madam. I beg your pardon. I'm advised that it was marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: We would like to tender this document in evidence, then, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then, the document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will continue to retain its exhibit number as 78.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, I'd like to ask you if you have an opinion as to why the El Mujahed Detachment existed.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I really have no idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. The Defence has been on its feet a lot today, but I don't think it's particularly useful to ask the witness his opinion. It's obviously the purpose of the witness is to advance his observations and facts he can tell us about. Opinions are rather for the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Robson. And I guess the Defence is here to be on its feet when it's necessary. If you have to be on your feet as many times, so be it. That's what you're paid for. Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, this gentleman was a member of the El Mujahed Detachment for two years, and I wanted to ask him some questions about the philosophy of the El Mujahed Detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think the ground of the objection is you're asking opinion evidence from a witness who's not an expert.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, I'm just asking him about his personal opinion, not as an expert, what his personal opinion was from his association with other members of the El Mujahed Detachment. But I can rephrase the questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think you could rephrase it without using the word "opinion," and it would be a perfectly legitimate question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, from your participation in the El Mujahed Detachment and your discussions with other members in the detachment, do you know why they were there in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, probably to help.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And to help whom?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: The Muslims in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And one second, Your Honour. May I have one second.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: In your experience and being in the unit, were they spreading any type of Jihad holy war?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before you ask the next question, I just want to get clarity to the previous answer. When you say they were helping the Muslims in Bosnia, help them in what, in doing what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To defend ourselves from the aggressor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I have a follow-up to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And who were the aggressors?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Sorry to interject. The question that I have, Your Honour, perhaps if we could just clarify, when the question was put to the witness, "Were they spreading any type of Jihad," I don't think it was established who "they" were specifically referring to. Perhaps if we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fair enough. But I guess Madam Sartorio now wants to make a follow-up to the question by the Bench. I guess you'll come back to the spread of --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour. I can ask that question now, and then do the follow-up as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: When I said "they," Mr. Alic, I meant the members and the commanders, all the members of the El Mujahed Detachment. Was it a purpose to start a Jihad or a holy war with your detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No, that was not the purpose.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when you mentioned a few minutes ago to the Judge about -- I believe you said you were helping the Muslims fight the aggressors. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And who -- I'm sorry. I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the witness because of the overlap.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you answer again, please, sir. The interpreters didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did say. So I said that they had come to help us defend ourselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And defend yourself against whom or what?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Against the aggressor; the Serbs, I say [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Were there any other aggressors, other than the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I couldn't say. Well, there were Croats later.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, during your time that you served in the El Mujahed Detachment, did your detachment fight alongside with other units of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: In the beginning, we didn't. We fought on our own. The Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I didn't see -- I don't see a completion to this answer. "We fought on our own. The Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina did." Did what?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: What do you mean, "on our own"? We were not alone. We were with the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: To your recollection, was there ever a time when the El Mujahed Detachment operated on its own?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, in the times that you were involved in combat with the El Mujahed Detachment, do you recall that there were other military units, formations, operating with you?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there've been a couple of questions along this line. Obviously, this is an important area, and I would ask my learned friend to proceed carefully in putting questions of this nature about whether the El Mujahed Detachment fought with anyone else. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Mr. Robson, I'm not quite sure -- I know it's a delicate area, but how else could the question be put, if the desired answer -- what needs to be established is whether or not this El Mujahedin fought alongside with some other unit or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the line of question now, I would have expected, is to first establish when, if indeed at all, the El Mujahed conducted combat operations, and then the questions could have flowed from there, rather than proceeding immediately to a question as to, "Do you recall whether there were other formations operating with you?" So in my submission, Your Honour, we're just getting a couple of steps ahead of ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio, you hear that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I heard it, Your Honour; however, I think it is a fair question. Just because we're getting into areas that may be going to the heart of some matters doesn't mean that questions -- if he can answer the questions, then I should be able to ask him whether his unit always participated with other units or not. That's not a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I didn't think so, because, I think, Mr. Robson, the witness has already indicated that the El Mujahed had come to help "them" fight the enemy. Now, if somebody's coming to help you fight the enemy, isn't it legitimate to find out whether you indeed fight together?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour, of course, it's legitimate. But the objection I had was putting it to the witness, every time they were fighting together. Essentially, that's where I saw the questions leading, and I thought just to put my own objection on record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. It is noted. I think if you can be any more careful than you have been so far, please try to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I will, Your Honour, it's just I do have a basis for asking that question. It's didn't come out of the blue. That's why I would like to pursue it a little bit further with the witness, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, you were involved in a number of combat operations with the El Mujahed Detachment; is that -- sorry. That's a leading question. Were you involved in a number of combat operations with the El Mujahed Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I'm going to be asking you about some of those operations which were discussed in the last few days in terms of proofing in the presence of team members; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And in the operations that you'll be discussing and telling the Court about today, in all of those operations, did the El Mujahed Detachment operate with other military units?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, if I showed you a prior statement that you made, would that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Would that help refresh the recollection of the witness, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Robson's point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry about this, Your Honour. But you did offer the opportunity for us to stand up whenever we thought there was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, indeed. That's why --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: -- a point to be made. Your Honour, obviously, the Prosecution is conducting its examination-in-chief. It's not a time for cross-examining its own witnesses. I would suggest that putting the witness's own statement to him at this stage will inevitably be leading him as towards an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not trying to impeach the witness. He said he didn't know, and I'm trying to refresh his recollection with a statement that he gave in 2005.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio, you know, you're referring the witness to discussions that you had with the team outside court. Don't you think that before you give him that statement, you should take him through, one by one, each of those comments, and then deal with each one of them so that his memory can be jogged? I think it would be helpful that way, then you would stay away from supposedly leading or impeaching or cross-examining.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. That is an excellent suggestion, Your Honour, and I'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, after your -- when was your first combat with the El Mujahed Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know the date when we had this first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could I ask that Map number 9 from the Court binder be put up for the witness, please. While that's happening, I can ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: You say you don't recall when it was. Was it -- can you give us any type of estimation in terms of a month, or would --

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. Approximately, it was perhaps in July or in August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Of which year, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1993, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you describe for the Judges what was the purpose of the operation and what you did, and if you could also draw on the map where you started, where you were located at the beginning of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess we're going to introduce him to the map first, and let him identify this map and understand it and see.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we just zoom in on this map a bit?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you zoom in on the map, itself, the center of it perhaps. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you see it now, Mr. Alic? Where was --

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, slightly better, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you recognise that map? Is this a map that is known to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, where was the command headquarters for the El Mujahed Detachment, if you see the place on this map?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I see the place. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what's the name of that place?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Poljanice. This hamlet has some other name, but I don't know. I call it Poljanice.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: For the sake of the record, could the witness put the number "1" next to the village of Poljanice?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, walk us through that first combat, if you would.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, from Poljanice we set off to Rasimulje [as interpreted], up here --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Simulje.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and then we continued. [Marks] We went in this direction. There are some fir trees here, and there's the village of Radonjici. [Indicating] That's more or less it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: We need to mark a couple of numbers along the way. Could you put a number "2" next to the place Simulje.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Simulje, number 2. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. And "3" around where you mentioned fir trees.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those trees here, number 3; and the village of Radonjici, that's number 4. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is there a name for the area where the fir trees were; do you know?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: It's near the place called Radonjici. In fact, there are these pine trees here. That's what it says here. It's a place called Borovi.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you know how many kilometres it is between Poljanice and Radonjici, approximately?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know how many kilometres it is. Well, perhaps a few kilometres more, perhaps a few less. I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court how long this operation took?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: When we set off or when we engaged in action?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, why don't you, again, walk us through it. Did you engage in action in Simulje?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. When we arrived there in front of the lines, when shooting broke out, it didn't last for long, perhaps ten or 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And then did anything happen at the area that's been marked Borovi?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No, no, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And -- okay. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: The lines were here behind Simulje, that area. Perhaps one kilometre away, you wouldn't find anyone there. [Indicating]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: How many members of the El Mujahed Detachment were you with during this operation?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, I said, at the beginning, there were 20 or 30 of us, but we weren't alone there. The ABiH was there, too, and they were both to the left and to the right of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And do you recall which units of the ABiH were with you?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, during -- I believe you said this was sometime, you said, in the summer. Was this in the summer of 1993, or July or August, you said?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The witness said "August 1993."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I thought he said "July or August."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: "Plus/minus August."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In those two months.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: But from the time that you joined the detachment in May of 1993 to this combat, were there any other combats in between?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: To your knowledge, during the entire summer, so June, July, and August of '93, were there any other combat operations in that area?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. Perhaps there were other operations, perhaps not. I can't remember. In 1993, well, I don't know whether there were any other operations in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did you and your detachment participate in any other operations in the summer of 1993 in this area?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: So this was the first one, and there were other such operations. But was that in 1993 or 1994, I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And during this operation, from whom were you taking orders?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, who was your first commander, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Abu Haris.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And do you recall any other persons who were in command of the El Mujahed Detachment at that time?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was Abu Haris at the time, there was Vahidin, and there were several other Arabs. But as far as I know, these persons were the most important ones.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: At the end of the operation, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, we went to Poljanice.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when you were at Poljanice, do you know who was in command of the detachment there?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, it was Abu Haris at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did Abu Haris have a title, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I know he was our emir. That's what we called him, "Emir."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, after this operation, did the command of the El Mujahed Detachment move?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, it did move. I don't know when. It moved to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And just one more question, Your Honour, because I understand we're getting close to the break. I would like to tender the map -- capture the markings on the map and then tender it into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The captured markings on the monitor is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit number 91.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Just one more question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio, what time did we start? We started at 4:00.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: 4.00. My case manager handed me a note, saying we're ready for a court break, but one more question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, before -- when the El Mujahed Detachment was at Poljanice and then when it moved, as you just said, to Zenica, did the command change? Did the command of the detachment change at all?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It remained -- or rather, the same emir was there. Nothing particular happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Did your role or duties change at all?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: In your experience, did the -- did the operation of the detachment, the daily operations, did that change at all?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, not really.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: At this point, Your Honour, I was going to show Mr. Alic some photographs, which might take -- a series of photographs. If you want me to start now, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would this then be a convenient point to take the break?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I think it would, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, Your Honour. Your Honour, at the court break, I was speaking with the court usher, because the next thing I would like to do is show this witness a series of photographs of persons, and I understand that a previous witness has already identified -- put the names to some of these photographs. But the court usher thought it would be the best thing at this point to tender the whole booklet of photographs and get that into evidence as one number, and then we'll have the witness go through the photographs and give the names of all of them and tender it as one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine. As you please, madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: For the record, the PT number is P061571, and the ERN, would you like? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you want them to admit it right away, or do you want to take him through them first before you tender them? Maybe you want to take him through them.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. I think that would be the best thing, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, I would like to take you through the photographs, starting with the photograph on page 1 of this booklet of documents, and ask if you can identify this person.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I can recognise this person.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what is his name?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: His name was Sheikh Enver.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I don't want to ask you this question for each one of these photographs, but was this person a member of the El Mujahed Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: He arrived at the very end. He wasn't with us from the beginning. He arrived at the end.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And the second photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. The question had been "but was he a member of the El Mujahed." Was he a member even when whatever time he arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was with us when we arrived there, for three or four months, approximately [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And he was a member of the El Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, he was with us. As to whether he had been entered on a list, as to whether this was on paper, I don't know. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. The interpreter can't hear the speaker.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- it says: "Sheikh Saban was with us when we arrived, for three or four months." I can't see it. I lost that part now. However, the witness said: "At the end of the war, for three or four months." So could we clarify this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. Can we clarify that? Earlier on the transcript, I have, when he first mentioned the name "Sheikh Enver," and you're also talking about Sheikh Saban. If you look at line 6 of page 73, what we have there is "Sheikh Enver." And at line 25 of the same page, you're referring to Sheikh Saban.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. That's the same person. The witness said "Sheikh Enver," I said "Sheikh Saban," but it's the same person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know him as "Sheikh Enver." That's what we called him, but I don't know his real name.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I do apologise for this mistake, but the purpose of my objection was to the translation. I objected to the translation, because the witness said the person appeared at the end of the war. The transcript said something different, so I would like that to be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. With respect to the names, understand, we don't know these people. So for us, if you say "Sheikh Enver" and somewhere else, "Sheikh Saban," these are two different people? Okay. That's solved. Madam Sartorio, can you clarify that point about that Madam Vidovic says is not clear about exactly when he came at the end of the war and what happened at the time?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I will ask him questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, do you recall where you were -- excuse me, where the El Mujahed Detachment was located when this person joined or when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, we were at Vozuca at the time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you answer, Mr. Robson is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Obviously, the Prosecution was instructed just to clarify that point, and I think we just strayed on to a different issue. So, perhaps, if before we deal with that fresh issue, if we could just clarify the business about when Sheikh Enver arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm trying, Your Honour. I'm trying to ask the witness as a matter of location to set some background, so that maybe he will have -- be able to place a date with a place. I'm not moving on to a separate matter. I'm trying to establish a time frame when this Sheikh Enver may have arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Sartorio. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: When is the first time that you saw Sheikh Enver?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: When we were at Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: When you say "we were at Vozuca," were at you the headquarters, or in the field, or where?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: We were in the field, 13th kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: When you say "13th kilometre," were you in the middle of operations or what was at 13th kilometre?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what the inhabitants said. They called this on the basis of the distance, in kilometres. I don't know the real name. There was some kind of accommodation there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: There was accommodation for the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, we couldn't stay in private houses, so we had to have a few locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Well, since we are going to be talking about this location in more detail later, let's establish it now. When you say "13th kilometre," what do you mean? Thirteenth kilometre from where?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, from the town of Zavidovici; so the first, the second, the third kilometre --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. So this is --

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: -- there's the fifth kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Up to the 13th; correct?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So this is an area that is referred to as "13th kilometre"?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: It's called "Kamenica," that area, but it's 13 kilometres from the town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what was at this area?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Nothing. We were just billeted there, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: When you say "we were just billeted there," who is "we" and what were you doing there?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, we, from the El Mujahed Detachment, we slept there, we rested there, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And did you sleep in buildings?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, there were two or three houses and a few tents.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So is that where you would go after, for instance, an operation?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Occasionally. Sometimes we would, and sometimes we wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Was this considered a command post for the El Mujahed Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, did you see Mr. Abu Haris at this camp?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know. He was killed. I don't know whether that was before that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, sorry. Certainly after his death, you wouldn't have seen him there. While he was still alive, do you remember seeing him at this place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He may have been there, but I couldn't tell you exactly whether that was indeed the case. I don't know when he got killed. I don't know whether he came to the camp. If he was alive, he was there. If he got killed earlier, then he couldn't have been there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So if you say he was alive, he would have been there. So does that mean that that's where -- did you meet other members of the El Mujahed Detachment at this location?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: What do you mean "other"?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, your fellow combatants, your fellow soldiers, members of the detachment. Did you meet others? Did you stay there for any period of time?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes. We did stay there for a certain period of time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And this is -- I believe you said this is the first place that you saw Sheikh Enver. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you recall the time of year that this was?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it was 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you recall any time period at all in 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Do you recall, did you ever participate in any combat action with Mr. Enver?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at the third photograph, the next page, the third, I suppose, page. There are three photographs on this page. Can you identify who this person is?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: That's Sheikh Enver.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And page 4. Now we're at page 4.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: It's the same person.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, I'd like you to look back at page 3, and then look again at page 4. Is it your -- is it your position that those are the same persons -- the same person, I should say.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Which is page 4 now?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Page 4 is ERN 0471-7266, if you have that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Is that the Sheikh, sir? Look at this person here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. That is not the same person.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: All right. I don't want to have the record be mixed up. Page 4 is ERN 7276, and we're on that page now? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you identify this person, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could the ERN number be shown, please, on the screen? Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I know this person, but I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And from where do you know this person?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, he would be there in Mehurici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when was this?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And do you have any -- can you narrow it any further in 1993?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: When I moved -- when I moved over to the detachment, I occasionally saw him there in Mehurici, but he was not with us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May we have the next photograph, please? It's 7267.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you identify this person, sir?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I think that that is the same person.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The next page, please, 7268. Am I going too fast for the Court, e-court? Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Are you able to identify this person, Mr. Alic?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am. This is Vahidin.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the next photograph, please, is 7269.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I think that is the same person also.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And would you just state the name for the record?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Vahidin.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And the next page, the photograph 7270. Can you identify this person?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know this person.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The next page, please, 0471-7271. There are two photographs on this page. Can you identify the person or persons in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I cannot. I don't know who these people are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know who the person in the forefront is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know this person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Just one question. You don't know this person's name, or have you ever seen this person?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know this person. I don't remember having seen that person ever.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. The next page, please, 7272. It contains two photographs. Can you identify anyone -- let's take the top photograph. Can you identify anyone in the top photograph?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I can. It is Safet Durgucic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the interpreter caught the last name properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what is he wearing?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: A green jersey.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The interpreter said, "If the interpreter caught the last name properly." Would you like to get the witness to repeat the of the person, please, and point at the person. I don't see a green jersey there. I see a blue one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Are you able to point on the ELMO to the person in the picture that you are speaking about?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: This is Durgucic, Safet. [Indicating]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I didn't see anything on my screen, a pointing. Okay. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: So this here is Safet Durgucic, and this is the Zenica mufti.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you don't know the name of the Zenica mufti, do you?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I didn't clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The name of the person who you identified in the coloured -- that you just identified a second ago, could you say his name very slowly?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Safet Durguti [phoen], as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May we take the next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we take the next photo, what is a mufti, a Zenica mufti?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I will ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us what a mufti is and what the Zenica mufti is?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: He lives in Zenica. That is something superior to a hodja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is a hodja?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hodja is someone who has completed the Medresa, and those who know more have the rank of mufti or muteris. So these are people with superior knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. You may proceed, Madam Sartorio. I'm sorry I took over from you, but I need to understand these terms.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Of course, yes, Your Honour. I was going to ask him if a mufti is an Islamic religion leader, if that's how he might characterise him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but the problem with that is that's putting words in his mouth.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'll withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry. The witness said, "No."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. May we see -- we're on the photograph at ERN 0471-7273.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask you: Can you identify anyone -- let's take the top photo. Can you identify anyone in the top photograph?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And which -- okay.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: This here is Abu Aiman, this person; and this other person is again the mufti of Zenica. [Indicating].

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The person in the white robe or the person in - I'm not sure if it's white - but did you just point to that person on the left of the screen?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And in the photograph down below, do you recognise or are you able to identify any persons?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you go back to the photograph? The person on the right of the screen, are you able to identify him, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This one here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't see. Yes, that one. This one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This person is Abu Aiman; this is the mufti; and this one, I don't know. [Indicating]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: In the picture that is at the bottom of this page, are you able to identify any persons in that picture?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May we take the next page, please? It's 0471-7274.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, are you able to identify any person or persons in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I do -- I am. This person here is Abu Haris; and this other one is Abu Malik, our interpreter. [Indicating]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And for the record, is there a person -- is that a microphone, do you see, in his hand? I don't think there would be any dispute that there's a microphone in his hand, if I asked that question. Is that who you've identified as Abu Haris?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Just for the record. Okay. May we have the next page. There are two photographs on this page.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Are you able to identify any person or persons in these photographs?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I am. This here is Abu Haris; and I believe this one is Vahidin, as far as I can see. [Indicating].

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, again, we have to be specific, because the transcript can't indicate when you say "this one." So could you describe the person on the left -- on your left, in terms of making the record?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: This here is Abu Haris. So this is Abu Haris, this person here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And who is on the right?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: And this other person is, I believe, Vahidin, as far as I can make out.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio, for purposes of the record, wouldn't it have been helpful to have the witness write their names?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: We discussed that, Your Honour, but I think for the sake of time, I even asked him in terms of spelling. So I'm not sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I did consider it. May we have the next page, which consists of four photographs, and ask you in the top photograph, are you able to identify this person?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is Abu Haris holding a microphone, then this is also Abu Haris. This is Abdul Malik. So this is, again, Abu Haris, Abdul Malik. It is Abu Haris and Abdul Malik. [Indicating]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And you mentioned Abu Haris is the one holding the microphone, is that correct, in all four pictures?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is that sufficient identification for the record, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's been identified. Whether we will be able to see this identification when we arrive at the judgement is another matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Sorry. Next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Are you able to identify this person?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And who is it?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: This is Abu Hamza.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may suggest, maybe if you mention the ERN number or the number, and we know -- at least we can relate the pictures that way later. The way it has gone, page 1, page 4, I'm not quite sure whether we are going to be able to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Madam Sartorio. Thank you. I'm sorry for that little intervention.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: No problem, Your Honour. We only have, I think, eight photographs left. The next page is 7277, the last four digits of the ERN number. Sorry. We just did that one. I apologise. Well, maybe we should go back, since we didn't put that number on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: 7277, again, who is this person, please?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Abu Hamza.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The next page, with 7278, who is this person?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: This is Abu Aiman.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the next page, 7279?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: This is Abu Maali.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And the next page, 7280?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: That is the same person.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The same person as whom? The name, please.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Abu Maali.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And number 7281?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: This is, again, Abu Maali.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And page 7282?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I think that, too, is Abu Maali.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: This person is Muatez.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know that person.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know this person, either.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I tender this lot of photographs in evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you going to tender everything, even those that he's not been able to identify?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, that is what the Court Officer suggested; and at some point, we can refer back to this trial exhibit when it comes to identifying the others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Well, then the photographs are admitted into evidence. May they please be given an exhibit number, a single exhibit number, for the entire collection.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. That will be Exhibit 92.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And that was PT061571; am I right?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alic, I'd like to take you to 1995, and ask you if you participated in any combat operations as a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment during that year.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us, approximately, when the first operation was that you participated in, what time of year?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, it's hard to remember. I think it was in 1995 at Vozuca. Whether it was in January or February, I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: -- as far as 1995 is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And we're going to go into Vozuca in a few minutes. I'm going to have you explain, in detail, the operation that you participated in. But at that time, do you recall --

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: -- sorry. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness said, "Yes."

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: In 1995, can you tell us if the El Mujahed Detachment had grown in numbers?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you tell us how much it had grown?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, there were quite a lot of us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can you try to be more specific for the Judges, when you say "quite a lot of us"?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the exact number, but there were quite a lot of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you have been more than a hundred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there were perhaps 200 or 300 of us, as far as I know. Perhaps there were more of us, and perhaps not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You estimate 200 to 300?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Something like that, as far as I know. I never counted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And where were -- where was the detachment centrally located, if there was a place?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: When you weren't out in the field, was there a type of command post or a headquarters for the detachment to gather?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No. We were resting somewhere in Vatrostalna; and as for a command post, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: You mentioned, "We rested in Vatrostalna." What does that mean, "we rested there"?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, some of us stayed there, some went home, and that location was left to go to the line and so on. Whoever was at home, for example, would go there and report, go to the line if it was necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: When you say "go there and report," do you mean Vatrostalna?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And is that where you would spend time -- when you weren't out in the field, in the middle of a combat operation, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, something like that. What do you mean, where did we go? Some of us stayed in Vatrostalna; others rested at home; and then others, when necessary, were at the lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, now, in terms of the Vozuca operation, could you explain to the Court the -- well, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Let me just, first of all, I'd like to bring up Map number 11 in the Court binder. Could we have the map up on the screen? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, can you --

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Can we zero in on the left-hand side of the map, where it seems to be a congestion right above -- okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the town of Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And can you tell us, from the town of Zavidovici, if there is -- what the line that is coming down, down the map and to the --

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, it's like this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: What's like this? Can you tell us the places that you recognise on this map, if you can see it?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I can recognise the town of Zavidovici; here's Potlecje; Poljica is here. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Perhaps, we can --

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, fine. Let's have a marker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Sartorio, if you could get the witness to point at these places that he's talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour. I'm trying to lay the foundation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. That's fine. That's not a problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: May I have a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we have the town of Zavidovici; Potlecje, number 1; Poljica, number two. 2. [Marks]. I can't see it very well. This is Potlecje; it's a place near Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which one, sir? I don't see what you're pointing at. Number 1?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Potlecje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And number 2?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 2, Poljica. Poljica. Well, it's at about more or less the fifth kilometre from town. It's the fifth kilometre. I can't see what it says here very clearly. Perhaps it's "Sinanovici." I don't whether we can enlarge this. I don't know if anyone can see any better than I can. I think it's Sinanovici, number 3; and to the right you have Lijevca, number 4; and then Borovnica, number 5; and then it follows until up the 13th kilometre, to Kamenica. So there's something missing on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes. And I think what we need to do --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: What we need to do at this point, Your Honour, is freeze -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We would like to capture this image of the map with the markings and tender it in evidence, because we need to move down the map and we'll lose these markings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May that page of the map be admitted into evidence and be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number 93.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. How did we call it, the map?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be referred to as Map number 11, Part 1; or Exhibit number 93, Part 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: To put it in context with the first map, would you please mark Borovnica again, please, as number 1.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Borovnica under number 5. [Marks] .

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And then keep going down to see what else--

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: This is Kamenica up next to Ravnjak; and the 13th kilometre is somewhere here. I don't know what this place is called. So this is the Borovnica route, Kamenica-Ravnjak up there. And somewhere around here, you should have the 13th kilometre, but I don't know what that part is called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I have a problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The witness keeps on saying "somewhere there," "somewhere here," and we don't see where he's pointing to.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I would like to know, can you see the 12th kilometre on this map, or do you see any markings of kilometres on where you are in the general location?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Again, I'm sorry, Madam Sartorio. You are talking about the 12th kilometre, and the witness is talking about the 13th kilometre. Let's stick to what the witness says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here I can see the number 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, the number 12, but you don't see a number 13, do you?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No, I can't see a number 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we be sure of the number 12, please, witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Would you mark the number 12, please?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Number 12, "6"

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And where would the number 13 kilometre be?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, a kilometre further on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And what was located at that 13th kilometre?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, two or three abandoned Serbian houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And was this -- was this also known, at 13th kilometre, under any other name?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know. There probably was some other name, but I don't know what it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is there a river nearby this 13th kilometre?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, what was it called? Gostovic or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you put a number "7" where you believe this spot is, the 13th kilometre?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, let's say it would be somewhere around here, one kilometre further on. [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Put a "7" there, please.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to get this map and the markings entered into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map will be entered. What will be the exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 94.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, in terms of the -- in terms of the operations or operation that you participated in 1995, would you please describe the first operation that you participated in with the El Mujahed Detachment?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date. When I spoke about it, the first one was not a real operation; and the first operation was a real operation, the one that involved actual combat.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. So we just need to characterise what the first -- not the first operation, but you've mentioned there was something that you did before you actually went into combat?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, it was a kind of reconnoitering operation from our lines. We just wanted to know what the situation was like up there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And when you -- okay. "Up there," can you tell us where "up there" was?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, the lines of the Serbs, held by the Serbs at Podsjelovo.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Let's go into, then, the first combat action. Describe for the Court where that action took place, if you recall, and how long it lasted. ?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Could we enlarge this? You have to scroll down a bit. A bit more, please, and a bit more. And now it's fine. So we passed through a place called Hajdarovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you see that on the map?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Would you mark it, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Just one minute. So we passed through Hajdarovici. Can we scroll the map down a bit?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I just have a question. Where did you start from, before you went there? You don't have to put it on the map. Just a town or a place.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: So we passed via Hajdarovici, and we arrived at a place called Livade, but I can't see that place indicated on the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: We're going to move the map a little bit and make it a little smaller so perhaps the area is larger, and see if you can make some markings.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I see Livade now. [Marks] So through Hajdarovici, we arrived at the village of Livade, and I've marked it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So that squiggle is Livade?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the village of Livade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Would you put a "1" there, please?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Now I've made a mess of it. Well, here it is. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And now tell us about the first combat action, if you can, where it took place.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, outside Livade, several metres from it, were our lines. Can I write on the map as I go along?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: So this is how the line went, and then up like this. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
