utterances.text: The interpreter can barely here the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Witness, will you speak loud when you do speak or keep quiet, because otherwise the interpreter doesn't hear you. Can you repeat what you have just been saying as you wrote the line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. This is more or less how it stretched, our line, that is, above the place called Lesici, up here. And where it went further on, I don't know. So this is Lesici here. [Indicating] So it stretched further on above Lesici to Imamovici, which is a neighbouring village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where is Lesici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Lesici here. I've marked it with a "2." [Marks] So this first simulated, this bogus action, that we carried out, this was from our starting lines. We never moved anywhere from there. This was just so that we could see where the heavy weaponry was. However, we did sustain some losses and some casualties. Some people were wounded in that action, in that action. I call it "action." It wasn't a real mission. We just had that action there, but the first real action was at trig point 706.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Is 706 anywhere on this map, that you can tell?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No, I don't see it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. So then just describe for the Court that action that took place at the 706, and what the purpose was, and how long it took.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: So this here was a reconnaissance action; and then some seven or eight months had elapsed after this preparatory and the reconnoitering actions, so that this real action actually took place sometime somewhere around here. [Indicating] . It was around trig point 706. There were some other trig point markings here, but I don't know them. Anyways, I was at trig point 706.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: You're not able to see -- are you able to see any numbers on this map?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No, not really.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And how long did the 706 elevation operation last? A couple of days or weeks?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: It lasted about four or five days.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And which units participated, if any, with you, with the El Mujahed Detachment, for this operation?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were some units of the army. I don't know what units of the army, but of the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And did you know if any prisoners of war were taken after this operation?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know about the first action, whether any people were captured during that action.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Let's talk about the next action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Wait a minute. Which is the first action? Are we talking about this action where you were at trig point 706? Did you conquer any prisoners of war during that action?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we did not. The first official action that was undertaken - so this was not an action; it was just some reconnoitering - the first real action was at elevation or trig point 706. That one lasted for four or five days, and the second action was at elevation 208.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you go to 208, did you have any prisoners of war captured during the action at 706?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You can move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Tell us about 208, please.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: So at elevation 706, we set out towards Cevaljusa, down towards Cevaljusa. That was the second official action. We approached Cevaljusa. We did not enter the village. We stayed for four or five days there. The fighting went on until we dug ourselves in there at those positions, and then we stayed there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And how long did that operation last?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Approximately, also three or four days. That is the usual.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Between the 706 action and the 208, where did you physically go to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do you mean, Madam Sartorio?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What does that question mean, Madam Sartorio? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: The questions means: Did he stay in the field, did he, did he go home, did he go back to any location?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Is it clearer now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean from elevation point 706, where did I go after that?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: After that operation ended, where did you physically go to?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: After the first action, that at elevation point 706, I went home for a rest.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And at some point did you receive -- how did you come about to participate in 208? Who contacted you?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, the emir did. They tell us that we should come, and then we go.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. And what is the name of the emir?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Abu Maali and Muatez were the emirs, as far as I know, then.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: When they tell you you should come and then "we go," where did they tell you to come to?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: First we reported at Vatrostalna. That was the meeting point, the concentration area; and then from there, we would go to the battle lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: During this time period of the 706 and the 208 operation, did you ever go to the 13th kilometre place?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know that I stayed up there. When I -- when I came back from my rest, I would stay there for a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Tell us about the next operation, please.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: The next operation, the second action, the one at elevation point 208, took place after I don't know exactly how much time, perhaps a month or longer. I'm not sure. So we reported at Vatrostalna; and from there, we proceeded to the 13th kilometre. Some of us came in the morning, others in the evening. And from that point, we -- at that point, we prepared ourselves to proceed up to the lines.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness what is some photos from pre-trial Exhibit 6165, PT6165 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, ma'am, what do we do with what's on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, sorry about that. Could we freeze it and give it an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The map on the screen is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit number 95.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like to show page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, can you tell us what is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: As far as I can make out, this is the 13th kilometre, where we were located.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And who is "we" located?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: We, the El Mujahed Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And was the detachment located here -- for how long was the detachment located here? For all of 1995?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, initially, when we arrived in Zavidovici, we were not billeted there right away. We stayed in Livade, up there in Livade. Some were in houses, some were in Vatrostalna, some were reconnoitering up there in Livade. Eventually, this location was found, and we were billeted there. It was nearer to the lines, so that we could reach the lines more quickly and so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness number 7, photograph number 7, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Mr. Alic, do you -- can you tell us what is depicted in this photograph and whether you saw this?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: After we had completed the second action, when I set out for my rest, we returned to the 13th kilometre, and that is when I saw this in passing, you know. I didn't count, but there were about ten men there. What happened afterwards, I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us where this place is on this particular photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, as far as I can make out, it was the 13th kilometre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, when you say you saw ten men there, what were these ten men doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were lying there. I don't know what they were doing. They were prisoners. I don't know what happened afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you say "ten men," are you referring to these people who are lying down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I didn't count; but as I stated in my statement, there were some ten or so people -- men there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand. But when you are talking about that number, you are referring to the people who are lying down? You are not referring to the people who are standing, like the one with a gun and the other one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise anyone in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And when you saw these bodies lying on the ground, do you know if they were dead or alive?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: What did you think when you saw this?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: What do I know? I don't know. I couldn't -- I couldn't really -- I had no idea in my mind, really, what to think about it. I couldn't imagine what might happen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you imagine what had happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say anything off the cuff.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I tender this photograph into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The photograph is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And also the first photograph that was number -- I understand there is a whole bundle of photographs, Your Honour, although I wasn't going to show all the photographs to the witness. I'm not sure if -- should we do that, as we did with the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. If you tender the whole lot, then the Registrar will just mark that only this one and the other one were identified.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 96.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: So when you saw the photograph we just -- when you saw the bodies on the ground, was that after the 208 operation or the 706?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: That was after the second action, after the second one.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Could you be more specific since we've been talking about these actions with different numbers?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was before the third action.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. Well, tell us about the third action now.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: That was the final action for the -- for taking Vozuca. That is when we indeed did take Vozuca. That was the last, the third action.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Do you recall when that last action started?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall the month. It may have been November. I'm not -- I can't be sure. Perhaps, it may have been November.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Okay. But I'd like to just set a little bit of a time frame. Between the operation that you just mentioned, where you went back to the camp after, and then this final operation, how much time elapsed?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe 15 days or a month, more or less.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Now, tell the Court briefly about the final operation.

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know what specifically they are interested in. What should I say?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: What was the purpose of the final operation? How long did it last?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: The purpose was to liberate Vozuca. It went on for about ten days, up until the Dayton Agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And during this operation, did the El Mujahedin Unit operate on its own, or were there any other units of the ABiH operating with them?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: There were other units.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask that same question for the other two operations that you spoke about. Were they operating with -- was the El Mujahed Detachment operating with units of the ARBiH?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: And after this operation, did you at any time return to the 13-kilometre location?

utterances.speaker: HASIB ALIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I'd like to show the witness -- oh, I guess we're out of time. I just have four short exhibits, Your Honour, I could cover hopefully in 15 minutes on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: On Monday?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You know, this witness was supposed to be one hour, Madam Sartorio. You've taken the entire day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, I know, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Is that, then, a convenient point for you to stop for today?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The matter is now being postponed to Monday, the 16th of July, at 9.00 in the morning in Courtroom II. You should be there at 9.00, sir. Okay? Thank you very much. Court adjourns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 16th day of July, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24
